prompt:
Style references only: the attached images set the painting style, the colours and the mood. Do not copy their content. Paint it as a concept artist's painted sketch sheet for a cozy, bright strategy game: loose hand-painted brushwork with visible strokes, soft painted light from a warm sunny afternoon coming from the front right, cheerful bright colours, a warm light cream paper background with a soft painted shadow under each object. It is a painting, not a 3D render, not low poly, not a game screenshot. Cozy and friendly like a storybook toy, never grim. No people, no text, no labels, no numbers, no letters, no watermark.

The sheet shows three small tangles of fallen twigs for a toy fortress game, side by side in one row, each lying on its own square grass tile one metre wide, seen in a three-quarter view from slightly above. The tiles lie loose on the cream paper like game pieces, their edges drawn as a slightly darker green line, so the size of each tangle reads against its tile. Every tangle has the same shape: a loose, friendly tangle of a few short branches and little twigs lying on the grass, about a third of a tile wide and only a hand tall, rounded and toy-like, nothing sharp. The three tangles differ only in their twig colours: Left: warm brown twigs with a lighter tan highlight. Middle: dry grey-brown twigs with a pale highlight. Right: dark brown twigs with tiny moss-green dabs on them. In front of the middle object, on its own tile, stands a small dark iron cannon on a low square plate that fills its tile: it is the size reference of the game. The twig tangle must read as much smaller than the cannon.
label: round 23 twiggy palette board
